title: Orchard and Promise
premise: Beatrix Crane, a wedding planner who swore off love after her own engagement collapsed, joins an anonymous pen-pal program at the orchard co-op where she's planning her sister's wedding—only to discover her assigned correspondent is Elias Vane, the estate lawyer contesting the very orchard her found family of farmworkers is fighting to inherit. Their letters, written without names, become the one place they're honest, even as their daytime selves battle over the deed. When identities are revealed mid-hearing, Beatrix must choose between protecting her heart and testifying to what she knows about the will's true intent. She risks everything in court, Elias withdraws his challenge, and the epilogue's harvest wedding ends with them exchanging vows of their own under the trees.
about_author: Jude Amberdale spent a decade coordinating weddings in cider country before trading clipboards for manuscripts, and still can't walk past an orchard in bloom without stopping. They write romances about people who build families out of stubbornness, shared labor, and second chances.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Orchard
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Juggling her sister's wedding plans and the farmworkers' fight against a contested will, Beatrix reluctantly signs up for the co-op's anonymous pen-pal program meant to ease community tensions. Her first letter lands with 'a stranger' who turns out to be Elias Vane, the opposing counsel. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness cracking open just slightly as writing to no one feels safer than talking to anyone.

chapters.title: Letters Between Adversaries
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Beatrix and Elias. By day they spar over depositions; by night their letters grow startlingly intimate—he confesses doubts about the case he inherited from his firm, she admits she stopped believing in weddings after being left at the altar. Neither knows who they're writing. Emotional beat: falling for someone through words while hardening against them in person.

chapters.title: What the Will Kept
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, then shattering into Beatrix's. Elias discovers a codicil suggesting the founder intended the orchard for its workers—and realizes his pen pal's phrasing matches Beatrix's testimony notes he glimpsed in discovery. At the pre-trial hearing, identities are exposed publicly: the letters were enemies all along. Beatrix feels betrayed; Elias must decide whether to bury the codicil or burn his career. Emotional beat: betrayal, then the choice that defines him.

chapters.title: Harvest Vows
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Elias presents the codicil, withdrawing the challenge at cost to himself, and the workers' inheritance is secured—but Beatrix, hurt, refuses to see him until her sister's wedding forces them together. During the ceremony she planned so carefully for everyone else, Elias reads their letters aloud as his own vow. She answers with the whole heart instead of pieces. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, and love chosen in full daylight.
